title: ‘Reach Out to Your Loved Ones and Give Them a Hug’: ‘A Family’ Director and Actor Call for Greater Emotional Awareness in Relationships
subtitle: Director Mees Peijnenburg explores the emotional impact of parental separation through the contrasting perspectives of two children; actor Pieter Embrechts urges audiences to reconnect with their loved ones
body_text:
Posted On: 28 NOV 2026 1:48PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2342995 Views: 54 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English
Goa, 28 November 2026 An invitation to reflect on family relationships, understand the emotional impact of parental conflict on children and reach out to loved ones was the central message shared by the director and actor of the Dutch film ‘A Family’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Director Mees Peijnenburg and actor Pieter Embrechts, spoke about emotional safety, fractured family relationships and the different ways children experience parental separation during a press conference held today. Emphasising the importance of self-reflection, director Peijnenburg described the film as an open invitation for adults and parents to become more aware of their actions and the impact they may have on children. He noted that people often have blind spots about their own behaviour and may not recognise how their actions affect those around them. He stressed that the film seeks to encourage greater awareness without passing judgment on the characters or their circumstances. Embrechts, who plays Jacob in the film, extended this message by encouraging audiences to reach out to the people closest to them. “I would love people to be calling or reaching out to their loved ones, the ones that are close to them, the ones that are nearest to you and give them a hug,” he said, adding that people need such connections, particularly in the present times. Reflecting on the inspiration behind the film, Peijnenburg revealed that the story was deeply personal, drawing partly from his own experience of growing up in a broken family. He wanted to explore what people seek when their world and family structures begin to fall apart. Through his research and observations, he identified emotional safety as a fundamental human need, particularly during periods of uncertainty and distress. “I believe we as humans are in search of emotional safety, especially when the world shakes, when the world around you starts trembling,” he explained. The director said he was also interested in exploring how different individuals experience the same events in contrasting ways. This idea forms the narrative foundation of A Family , which follows siblings Nina and Eli as they navigate their parents' separation. While both children experience the same family breakdown, they respond to it differently. Peijnenburg described Nina as a girl who internalises her emotions, likening her to a volcano with an inner storm, while Eli attempts to please everyone around him, becoming caught between his parents. Despite their contrasting responses, both children are ultimately seeking love and emotional security. Explaining his decision to narrate the story through the children’s perspective, Peijnenburg observed that cinema has paid comparatively less attention to how children and teenagers experience such circumstances. The film therefore places them at the centre of the narrative, exploring how they navigate difficult emotional realities while their parents grapple with their own pain. The film's visual language also formed an important part of the discussion. Responding to a question on the frequent isolated framing of Nina, even when she is physically present with her family, Peijnenburg said that it was a deliberate creative choice developed in collaboration with cinematographer Jasper Wolf. He explained that the visual approach was designed to present the children's individual experiences as separate emotional monologues that gradually develop into a dialogue. While Nina is often positioned in isolation within the frame, Eli is frequently shown through other people. The director explained that the filmmakers deliberately chose to focus on what the parents were not looking at, shifting attention away from their arguments towards the emotional consequences experienced by the children. “It's not necessarily about their fight. It's about the effect of the fight,” he explained. Peijnenburg also discussed the deliberate use of harsh daylight in emotionally intense scenes, rather than relying on conventional darker or cooler lighting. He said the intention was to create an open and naturalistic visual approach that exposed the characters' emotional realities without hiding or exaggerating them. Describing the approach, he said the filmmakers wanted to present the situations as they were, making the emotional experience more direct for viewers. Through the contrasting experiences of Nina and Eli, A Family examines the need for emotional safety, the consequences of parental conflict and the importance of recognising the perspectives of those around us. Rather than offering easy answers to family breakdown, the film invites audiences to reflect on their relationships, become more conscious of their actions and value the connections they share with their loved ones. The director and the actor expressed their appreciation for the opportunity to present the film at the 57th IFFI, thanking the festival for inviting them and sharing their work with audiences. The session was moderated by Ms. Sasmita .
